In that case, the corruption promised in the texts from those people would be what the Tatars caused of corruption in the lands, as in the era of Genghis Khan, and what he and his companions wrought in the world. And Allah knows best. End.

It is stated in *al-Jughrafiyya al-'Umumiyya* (General Geography), in the forty-seventh article on the mapping of Asia, concerning the lands of the Caucasians, i.e., the people of Kawh Qaf, i.e., Mount Qaf: In those regions this mountain extends like a great wall, and in it there are two passes called by the ancients the Caucasian Gates and the Albanian Gates. The first pass, the Caucasian Gates, was the one through which invasions of barbarians were feared against both the Roman and Persian states. Then the fortress that used to block this pass is called by different names among the ancients. As for the Albanian Gates, the most famous opinion concerning them is that they are the pass of Derbent along the shore of the Caspian Sea.

He then said: There is a famous story among the people of Kawh Qaf which indicates that this mountain was blocked by a great barrier that prevented the raids of the barbarians. This great barrier is sometimes attributed to Alexander, and sometimes to Anushirvan. They rely on remains still existing to this day, visible to anyone who wishes to see them.

The eighth note: Abu'l-Baqa' said: Gog and Magog are two foreign names, not declined because of foreignness (ajamiyya) and definiteness. It is permissible to pronounce them with a hamza and without a hamza. It was said: they are Arabic, so Ya'juj is on the pattern *yaf'ul*, like *yarbu'*, and Ma'juj is on the pattern *maf'ul*, like *ma'qul*. Both derive from *ajja al-zaliml* (the ostrich ran swiftly), or from *ajjat al-nar* (the fire blazed). They are not declined because of definiteness and feminine form, i.e., as a tribe, like Majus. The two words are from one root in derivation. On the foreign view, its morphology cannot be analyzed, and its pattern is considered only on the assumption that it is Arabic, as in the *Tadhkirat* of Abu 'Ali.

Al-Razi said: They differed as to which peoples they belonged to. It was said: they are from the Turks. It was said: Ya'juj is from the Turks and Ma'juj from the Jil and the Daylam. Then some people described them as short in stature and small in body. End.

Some researchers said: Behind a mountain of the Caucasus range, known to the Arabs as Mount Qaf, in the region of Dagestan, there were two tribes. One of them was called *Aquq* and the second *Maquq*, which the Arabs arabicized as Ya'juj and Ma'juj. They are known to many nations, and their mention occurs in the books of the People of the Book. From them descend many of the northern and eastern nations of Russia and Asia.

The ninth note: Those who did not require authenticity or even goodness in their compilations among the narrators have been lax in transmitting what is reported about Gog and Magog. Most of it is either from the Israelite narratives (*Isra'iliyyat*), or unacceptable reports (*munkarat*), or fabricated ones (*mawdu'at*). Among this is the hadith: "Gog is a people and Magog is a people. Every people has four hundred thousand peoples. No man of them dies until he sees a thousand males from his own loins before him, every one of whom has carried weapons..." etc. Ibn 'Adi related it in *al-Du'afa'* from Hudhayfah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: It is fabricated and unacceptable; Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-'Ukkashi is a liar who fabricates. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted it.

The Hafiz Ibn Jarir here related, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, a long and wondrous report about the journey of Dhu'l-Qarnayn, his building of the barrier, and how events happened to him. It contains great length, strangeness, and unacceptability regarding their forms, their attributes, their height, the shortness of some of them, and their ears.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from his father on this matter strange reports whose chains of transmission are not authentic. End.

So may Allah reward al-Bukhari with the best reward for rejecting those narrations and for making authenticity a condition for what is transmitted, for unacceptable reports have done the greatest harm to the Ummah. Whoever reads the introduction of Sahih Muslim will recognize the truth of his statement: "The transmitter of weak reports is a deceiver, sinful and misleading." And with Allah is the help sought.

The discussion of the explanation of His words, exalted is He:

[99] ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering.﴾

﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering.﴾ That is: it will be blown into it for the resurrection in the second creation. Then We will gather them for recompense and reckoning, a gathering wondrous, whose true nature none can fathom.

An imam said: The blowing into the Horn is a figurative expression for God raising people on the Day of Resurrection with a speed that nothing could represent except a blast on a trumpet, whereupon they are standing, looking on. It is incumbent upon us to believe in what has been reported concerning the blowing into the Horn, but it is not incumbent upon us to know what the true reality of that Horn is. Inquiry beyond this is vain and not permissible for a Muslim; that is, because it belongs to the realm of the unseen, meaning the matters hidden from us, whose realities we have not been charged with investigating.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[100] ﴿And We will present Hell on that Day to the disbelievers, [in] presentation.﴾

﴿And We will present Hell﴾, i.e., We will make it manifest and bring it forth. ﴿On that Day﴾, i.e., the day when We gather all creation together. ﴿To the disbelievers﴾, i.e., from among them, in that We will place them in a position where they see it and hear its roaring and its wailing in rage. ﴿[In] presentation﴾, i.e., a dreadful, awesome display whose extent cannot be measured.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The specification of the presentation to them, although it is in view of all the people of the gathering, is because it is for their sake alone. In presenting it to them and making them see what it contains of punishment and torment before entering it, there is an increase in wrath against them and a blow to them, because this is more effective in hastening distress and grief. And His exalted saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[101] ﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance, and who were not able to hear.﴾

﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance, and who were not able to hear.﴾ This is a figurative depiction of their blindness toward the signs that indicate His Oneness, or toward the Qur'an and reflecting on its meanings and perceiving them. And of their deafness toward the truth and following guidance. His words, Exalted is He, ﴿and who were not able to hear﴾ are more eloquent than "and who were deaf," because the deaf person may be able to hear if he is shouted at. These people are as if their hearing had been struck deaf, so there is no capacity in them for hearing. This is what al-Zamakhshari stated. There is another subtle point in describing them with the two clauses, by which you know that the second cannot be dispensed with in favor of the first, as some claimed. And that, as al-Shihab verified, is that His words, Exalted is He, ﴿are not able to hear﴾, since it indicates that they are like those who have lost the faculty of hearing, and one who is so only recognizes remembrance by sign, writing, or the like, which are perceived by sight, and he mentioned that their eyes are also veiled from looking at what indicates it. So they have no way at all to know His remembrance. This is of great eloquence.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The relative pronoun, meaning ﴿those whose﴾, is an adjective for the disbelievers, or a substitute or an explanatory apposition, brought to condemn them by what is in the scope of the relative clause, and to indicate its causality for the afflicting of what afflicted them of the exposure of Hell to them. For that is only because they did not use their faculties in what was presented to them in the world of the signs, and their turning away from them, although they were means of salvation from what they were tested with in the Hereafter.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[102] ﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors instead of Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.﴾

﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors instead of Me?﴾ This is a return to the opening of the surah in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and to warn those who say, "God has taken a son."﴾ [al-Kahf: 4]. It is of the type of "radd al-'ajuz 'ala al-sadr" (returning the end of a passage to its beginning), established in the science of badi' (rhetoric). The interrogative is used in a denunciatory sense (istifham inkari), denouncing what they did and rebuking them. The second object of "hasiba" (to think/suppose) is omitted, i.e., "Did they think that their taking [these beings] was beneficial to them?" Compare His saying: ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will become opponents to them﴾ [Maryam: 82], and as they said: ﴿Glory be to You! You are our Protector, not them﴾ [Saba': 41]. ﴿Indeed, We have prepared [a'tadna]﴾, i.e., We have readied, ﴿Hell as a lodging [nuzul] for the disbelievers.﴾ i.e., something they enjoy upon their arrival. The word "nuzul" is what is prepared for a guest (nazil), i.e., the one of weak standing. In it is a sarcastic metaphor (isti'arah tahakkumiyyah), as it treats what they are punished with in Hell, such as the zaqqum and the ghislin, as a hospitality extended to them.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In it there is a rebuke of them for their supposition and a mockery of them, since their taking those beings as protectors is of the kind of gathering equipment (i'tad al-'atad) and preparing provision (i'dad al-zad) for the Day of Return. It is as if it were said: "We have prepared for them, in place of what they prepared for themselves of readiness and stored provision, Hell as a readiness." In the mention of "nuzul" there is an allusion that beyond Hell they have punishment that is a model of it, i.e., because the guest does not settle in the house of hospitality, but moves on to what is a humiliation for him in his dwelling place. Thus it is a warning that they will taste what is more severe.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[103] ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of those most lost in their deeds?﴾ [104] ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think that they are doing well in work.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 104] [105] ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the verses of their Lord and in the meeting with Him, so their deeds have become worthless, and We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105] [106] ﴿That is their recompense: Hell, for what they disbelieved and took My verses and My messengers in mockery.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 106].

﴿Say: Shall we inform you of those most lost in their deeds?﴾ ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world﴾ [Al-Kahf: 104] meaning: it went to waste and became void. ﴿while they think that they are doing well in work﴾ [Al-Kahf: 104]. ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the verses of their Lord﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105] meaning: those which their messengers brought with the call to act upon them. ﴿And in the meeting with Him﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105] meaning: with the Resurrection, the reckoning and the recompense. ﴿So their deeds have become worthless﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105] because of their aforementioned disbelief. ﴿So We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105] meaning: We will hold them in contempt and will not give them any measure or consideration, because the basis of weight is righteous deeds, and these have utterly become void.

﴿That﴾ [Al-Kahf: 106] meaning: the matter is that. His saying ﴿their recompense is Hell﴾ [Al-Kahf: 106] is a sentence explaining it, or ﴿that﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and the sentence is its predicate (khabar), with the returning pronoun (al-'a'id) omitted; meaning: their recompense is by it. Or ﴿their recompense﴾ is the predicate, and ﴿Hell﴾ is an explicative apposition ('atf bayan) to it. ﴿For what they disbelieved and took My verses and My messengers in mockery﴾ [Al-Kahf: 106] meaning: mocked at by them. That necessitates intense abhorrence, wrath and severe punishment.

Then He explained what is the good reward awaiting their opposites, with His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[107] ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them will be the Gardens of Paradise (Firdaws) as a lodging.﴾ [108] ﴿Abiding therein eternally; they will not desire any removal from it.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 107–108]

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them will be the Gardens of Paradise (Firdaws) as a lodging.﴾ ﴿Abiding therein eternally; they will not desire any removal from it.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 108] That is: no transferring (taḥawwul), because they have reached perfection in its bliss. So there is no longing for them in anything beyond it. In this there is an alert to the intensity of their desire for it and their love for it. Although one might suppose, regarding someone who dwells permanently in a place, that he would grow weary of it or tire of it, He informs that they, despite this permanence and everlasting eternity, do not choose any change from their station.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[109] ﴿Say: "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."﴾

﴿Say: "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord"﴾, i.e., for writing them down: ﴿the sea would be exhausted﴾, i.e., despite its abundance, and nothing would remain of it: ﴿before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾, i.e., because they are without end, so they do not run out the way finite things run out.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In attributing "the words" to the name of the Lord, which is itself attached to His pronoun ﷺ in both places, there is an exaltation of what is attributed and an honouring of the one to whom it is attributed, which is not hidden. The explicit mention of "the sea" and "the words" in place of a pronoun serves to increase the affirmation. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿even if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾, i.e., the like of the sea as help and addition, would also be exhausted.

Abu al-Su'ud said: This is a statement from Him, Exalted is He, not part of the dictated speech; it is brought to confirm its meaning and to verify what it indicates, with added emphasis and affirmation. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if whatever trees on earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ [Luqman: 27]

Note:

The verse indicates that He, Exalted is He, has never ceased to speak whenever He wills and as He wills, and that His words have no end. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, and others among the imams said: Allah has never ceased to be speaking whenever He wills, and He speaks by His will and power, speaking one thing after another. This is the doctrine of the early community (salaf), the leaders of the Sunnah, and many of the people of kalam, such as the Hashimiyya, the Karramiyya and the followers of Abu Mu'adh. Other groups besides these say: speech is an attribute of essence and of action; He speaks by His will and power, a speech subsisting in His essence. This is what is understood of the attribute of speech for every speaker. Every living being described as speaking, such as the angels, humans, jinn and others, their speech must subsist in themselves, and they speak by their will and power. Speech is an attribute of perfection, not of deficiency, and whoever speaks by will is more perfect than one who does not speak by will. How then could the created being be described by attributes of perfection while the Creator is not?

As for the Jahmiyya and the Mu'tazila, they say: He has no speech subsisting in His essence; rather His speech is created and separate from Him. The Kullabiyya say: He speaks with a speech over which He has no power, and which is not by His will. The Ash'ariyya say: speech is one meaning that does not divide or multiply. All these are false doctrines, contrary to the Book, the Sunnah and the consensus of the early community. They are innovations built on one root principle, namely their claim that the Lord is not the subject of voluntary matters, so no speech or action subsists in Him by His choice and will. This root is false and contrary to transmission and reason. The noble Qur'an proves its falsehood in more than a hundred places. As for the sound hadiths, they cannot be enumerated in this matter. The correct position on this and related questions, which is the doctrine of the early community and its imams, is that He, Glorified is He, has never ceased to speak whenever He wills; He speaks by His will and power; His words have no end; He called out to Musa with a voice that Musa heard, and He called him only when he came, not before that; the voice of the Lord is not like the voices of His servants, just as His knowledge is not like their knowledge and His power is not like their power; He, Glorified is He, is distinct from His creation in His essence and attributes; nothing of His creation is part of His essence and attributes subsisting in His essence, and nothing of His essence is part of His creation. The statements of the deniers (ahl al-ta'til) and of those who claim union (ittihad), who deny the essence, the attributes, the speech or the actions, are false; and the statements of those who hold indwelling (hulul), who say that He indwells in essence and attributes, are false. This is what Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyya, may mercy and good pleasure be upon him, conveyed.

He also said, regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord"﴾ and the rest of the verse: The words of Allah have no end. This is an infinite regress that is permissible, like the infinite regress in the future, for the bliss of Paradise is lasting and has no end. Thus, there is nothing but that after it there is something else, without end.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[110] ﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is but one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord."﴾

﴿Say﴾, i.e., to these polytheists and disbelievers among the People of the Book: ﴿I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is but one God﴾, i.e., I have been singled out for revelation and distinguished from you by it. ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ (p-4123), i.e., fears the return to Him, or hopes to meet Him and see Him, or [hopes for] His good reward and recompense: ﴿let him do righteous work﴾, i.e., in itself, fitting for that which is hoped for, and that is what conforms to the Law of God. ﴿And not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, i.e., of His creation, by overt association, as those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him did. Nor by hidden association, as the people of showing-off (riya') do, and whoever seeks by it a reward of praise, acquiring wealth, or standing.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The preference for placing the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun in both places, together with mention of the title of Lordship, is for added affirmation, and to indicate that the title is the reason for the command and prohibition, and for the obligation to comply, in doing and in refraining.

The verse indicates, as Ibn Kathir said, that an accepted deed has two pillars: that it conforms to the revealed Law of God, and that it is sincere, intended for the Face of the Exalted, not mixed with anything else. Calling showing-off "minor shirk" is established in the Sunnah, and it is authentically reported there that deeds are nullified by showing-off. Showing-off's inclusion in the verse, in terms of the generality of its meaning, is valid, although the context concerns overt shirk, because the address is to the deniers. And God the Exalted is the Granter of success and the Helper.
